The reachable Python advisories are cleared. The Angular advisories that have no fixed release can't be cleared by a version bump, so they remain. `recon_qa` passes with no new divergences and the app's `run_tests` is green, but that suite is only a smoke check. I also ran a slice of the real pytest suite against the new lockfile. Three tests failed because `tesseract` and `unpaper` aren't installed here.

I did not re-run the full `security_scan` after the final lockfile update. The last `scan_diff` against HEAD showed no new advisories, and I have not checked it for leftovers.

**Python (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` regenerated with uv)**

| Package | Change |
|---|---|
| django | 5.1.7 → 5.2.19 |
| nltk | 3.9.1 → 3.10.4 |
| bleach | 6.2.0 → 6.4.0 |
| jinja2 | 3.1.5 → 3.1.6 |
| pytest (dev only) | 8.3.4 → 9.0.3 |
| filelock | 3.17.0 → 4.2.10 on Python ≥3.11 and 3.20.4 on 3.10. 4.x needs Python ≥3.11 and the project still declares 3.10, so I split by marker instead of raising `requires-python`. |
| cryptography (transitive) | 44.0.2 → 50.0.2, forced with a `constraint-dependencies` entry. |
| django-allauth | 65.4.1 → 65.14.3 (not on the scan's list). |

The `cryptography` pin forced fido2 1.x to 2.x. allauth 65.4 crashed on import with fido2 2.x (`manage.py check` failed with an `AttributeError` in `allauth.mfa`), so I moved allauth to the first 65.x release that tolerates it, 65.14.

One test change: `test_pre_authenticate` mocked `allauth.core.ratelimit._consume_rate`, which no longer exists. I pointed it at `allauth.core.internal.ratelimit.consume`.

With the new lockfile, `manage.py check` passes apart from the tesseract warning. The classifier tests (the nltk path), the paperless tests and the API tests pass. The suite hits the missing binaries in the consume tests and the two `test_binaries*` checks. I skipped `zxing-cpp` and `psycopg-c` when installing the venv because `zxing-cpp` failed its hash check, so the barcode tests were not run.

**npm (`src-ui`)**
- The Angular packages (`common`, `core`, `compiler`, `forms`, `localize`, `platform-browser`, `platform-browser-dynamic`, `router`, `compiler-cli`) now resolve to 19.2.25, which clears every Angular advisory that has a fix.
- `uuid` is now 11.1.1.
- `webpack` is overridden to 5.104.1 in the new `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, because the installed pnpm no longer reads the `pnpm` field in `package.json`. I moved `onlyBuiltDependencies` there too so it still applies.

**Still open:** the Angular advisories NEAT lists with no fixed release. That covers `@angular/common` (HttpTransferCache and XSRF handling), `@angular/core` (i18n XSS, hydration) and `@angular/router` (SSR denial of service). 19.2.25 is the newest 19.2.x I could resolve. Clearing them would mean replacing Angular or waiting for upstream fixes.

NEAT flagged all of these as "imported, no call path to changed code", so none was shown to be exercised at runtime.
